an3.80:1.3: Ānanda is referring to [sn6.14:5.3](); see there for notes on Sikhī and Abhibhū.
an3.80:3.5: Elsewhere in the Pali we usually hear of a single world system, which I translate as “solar system” or a “ten-thousand-fold galaxy”.
an3.80:4.1: _Virocanā_ (“dazzling ones”) is a term for the shining heavenly bodies, especially the sun ([ud6.10:5.3]()).
an3.80:4.2: The “four continents” are mentioned occasionally ([sn55.1:1.3](), [thig16.1:39.1]()), but this (with its parallel at [an10.29:2.2]()) is the only early passage that mentions the four continents.  Pali texts here read _aparagoyāna_, “west of Goyāna” (“cow-cart”), but no Goyāna is found elsewhere in this sense. The normal Sanskrit spelling is _aparagodānīya_, “bestowal of cows”, i.e. a land abundant in the wealth typified by cows. Now, _godānīya_ is a mere verbal variation of _godāvarī_, the name of the famed river that arises near Nashik, not far from modern Mumbai on the west coast ([snp5.1:2.3]()). Lands further west were reached by ship from that shore, and the river sometimes loaned its name to the place and people of Nashik. I propose we emend to “west of Godāvarī”.
an3.80:9.1: The lack of vocative in what follows indicates that this was not addressed to anyone, per Thai editions.
